findings.message: The retained-write matrix says POST/PATCH documents, decisions, communications and inquiries are retained with 'actual create/update action'. The closed raw-write field table (lines 181-189) allows only filename for documents and 'None' for decisions, communications and inquiries. A document POST therefore cannot supply its NOT NULL kind/origin/storage_key/content_hash, so generic create is effectively unavailable. This is coherent as 'permission preserved, unsafe effect removed', but the matrix never states that outcome. Name the expected result (e.g. permitted role reaches validation, unknown/protected field rejected with existing 400/422) for each retained create whose writable set is empty or not viable, so Inspector positives/negatives are not guessed.

Every in-scope candidate is evaluated before selection, worst flag first. So one PRESCRITO_OPERACIONAL candidate lacking qualified incident input makes the 503 apply to the whole pool's claim, not just one case. The ADR does not say this explicitly, and it does not specify behaviour for claim-context GET or GET cases/:id/risk (200 with the flag vs 503) in the same condition. The incident input is also not modelled in the CTG supplement or adapter contract. State the pool-wide effect, the inventory visibility of the blocking case and the GET/risk-read outcome.

WF-RAIT-002 (status approved) labels the §4.3 clock-A table 'ladder proposta' and says the 360-day track 'escala proporcionalmente'. A has no PRESCRITO_OPERACIONAL stage. parameter-catalogue line 209 says OD-004/005/006 values enter as version 1 'proposta'. Calling rait.ladder.A an 'approved' transcription without stating the new row's catalogue status and source label risks silently promoting a proposed ladder to vigente. Record the row status exactly as sourced. C (§4.2) is unaffected.

RaitRiskSnapshot.clocks carries only {clockCode, flag}. It has no per-clock applicability or ceilingOn. So the 'explicit not-applicable' display at line 78 cannot be represented per clock, and CaseHeader's per-clock ceiling_on must come from a separate raw clock read at a different source instant. Either add applicability/ceilingOn to the snapshot element, or state that the header combines the two reads and how it handles inconsistency between them.

Editorial: the three new errors are said to be 'specified in ADR0048/49', but CASE_POOL_UNRESOLVED409 is specified in ADR0047. The following sentence still says 'Neither discloses a candidate' for three errors.
